Main Points
⏺ DEX limit orders often rely on executors or special order-flow designs

⏺ This post explains how on-chain limit orders actually work

1️⃣ Why It’s Different — on-chain trading doesn’t have a centralized matcher like a CEX order book.
2️⃣ Common Designs — off-chain orderbook + on-chain settlement, or smart-contract conditional execution.

A DEX limit order isn’t a simple “CEX button” — it’s an execution service. Price is controlled, mechanics are deeper.

How much would Bitcoin need to be worth to match the real purchasing power of $1 million from different eras?

The equivalent of $1 million in 2023 purchasing power would require Bitcoin to reach roughly $1.5 million per BTC (around 2036), while matching the purchasing power of $1 million in 1983 would require a price of approximately $6 million per BTC (around 2043). 

In other words, simply becoming a "Bitcoin millionaire" will gradually mean less as inflation erodes the value of money. To preserve the purchasing power of a historical $1 million, Bitcoin would ultimately need to trade well above the $1 million mark.

People think cancel culture is something new, invented in the last ten years by people with smartphones. It's not. In Elijah's day they didn't cancel you with a hashtag or a mob in your comments section. They sent soldiers. Jezebel hunted down the prophets of God one by one, and the message to everyone watching was simple: stay quiet, stay neutral, and you get to stay alive.

Most of the people obeyed. Faith went silent. Not because believers stopped believing, but because the cost of speaking became too high. Sound familiar? Today God’s followers are told the same thing in a thousand polite ways. Keep your faith private. Don't bring it into politics. Don't be combative. Stay in your lane. It is the exact same pressure Elijah faced, just wearing a nicer suit.

So what did the faithful do when Jezebel hurled her threats? They hid. A man named Obadiah took one hundred prophets, tucked them away in caves, and kept them alive on bread and water. And hear me carefully, because this is important. God Himself provided those caves. There was mercy in the hiding places, and there was a season for them. God is not cruel; He knows how to preserve His people through the storm. There are times when God will shelter you.

But here is the thing. Staying in the cave does not win the culture war. A hidden prophet stays alive, but a hidden prophet does not call down fire. He does not confront Ahab. He does not rebuild the broken altar. Israel was not turned back to God by the hundred who survived in the dark. It was turned back by the one who walked out into the daylight and stared danger in the eye.

And watch the order of what happened when he stood strong, because we always get it backwards. In 1 Kings 18, Elijah stood alone first. He rebuilt the broken altar first. He drenched the whole sacrifice in water and looked like a complete crazy man in front of everyone first. Only then did the fire fall. Today, we reverse it. We wait for the crowd before we obey. We want the revival before we are willing to stand. But the mountain wasn't crowded with God’s allies when the fire came. There was one man facing a nation that had already gone fully after Baal.

So stop counting heads. Stop waiting to stand until the truth is safe and popular, because that day is not coming. The fire follows obedience; obedience does not follow the fire. There is a time God shelters you, and there is a time God says to get out of the cave. 

I wrote The Elijah Mandate because the caves are full and the mountain is empty. That must change!
